story_description: As a user with multiple concurrent CLI sessions, I want to see visual badges indicating which sessions have unread events so I can quickly identify which sessions need my attention without manually checking each one.
task_description: Create and integrate the CountBadge component into SessionRow to display unread event counts. The badge should appear when unread count is greater than zero, be hidden for the currently active session, and follow the design system styling conventions.
atom_description: Implement the visual badge component that displays unread event counts on session rows in the sidebar. This includes the CountBadge view component, conditional visibility logic, and proper integration with the existing SessionRow layout structure.
problem_statement: Users managing multiple concurrent CLI sessions have no visual indicator of which sessions have accumulated new events since they last viewed them. This forces users to manually click through each session to discover activity, wasting time and causing missed important events in background sessions.
scope_in: CountBadge SwiftUI view component implementation with configurable count display
Conditional badge visibility logic based on unread count and active session state
Integration of CountBadge into existing SessionRow component layout
Badge styling following design system color tokens and typography
Accessibility labels for screen reader support on badge element
scope_out: Unread count calculation logic from event stream (handled by T001)
Badge animation or transitions when count changes (future enhancement)
Badge click interactions or navigation behavior
Notification system integration for OS-level alerts
assumptions: UnreadTracker service exists and provides currentUnreadCount(for: sessionId) method
SessionStore.currentSessionId property is available for active session detection
Design system includes color tokens for badge background and foreground
SessionRow already has a horizontal layout structure that can accommodate the badge
SwiftUI environment provides access to current theme for badge coloring
constraints: Badge must not exceed 20pt width to prevent layout overflow in narrow sidebars
Badge must be hidden rather than showing 0 to avoid visual clutter
Must use design system primitives rather than custom styling
Must support VoiceOver accessibility for vision-impaired users
Must not cause layout shifts when appearing or disappearing
functional_requirements: FR1: CountBadge displays integer count value when initialized with count > 0
FR2: CountBadge renders as empty view when count equals 0
FR3: SessionRow shows CountBadge only when session has unread events AND is not the current session
FR4: Badge displays 99+ for counts exceeding 99 to prevent layout overflow
FR5: Badge background uses accent color from design system theme
FR6: Badge text uses contrasting foreground color for readability
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Badge render time must not exceed 1ms to maintain 60fps scroll performance
NFR2: Badge accessibility label must include exact count for screen readers
NFR3: Badge must maintain visual consistency across light and dark themes
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create CountBadge.swift in Blaze/Sources/DesignSystem/Components with View protocol conformance
Step 2: Implement CountBadge body with Text view displaying formatted count string
Step 3: Add capsule background shape with design system accent color fill
Step 4: Implement count formatting logic to show 99+ for large values
Step 5: Add conditional @ViewBuilder logic to return EmptyView when count is 0
Step 6: Add accessibilityLabel modifier with descriptive count text
Step 7: Modify SessionRow.swift to inject UnreadTracker dependency
Step 8: Add computed property to SessionRow for shouldShowBadge based on unread count and active state
Step 9: Insert CountBadge in SessionRow HStack after Spacer and before HoverButtons
Step 10: Verify badge visibility toggles correctly when switching sessions
data_model_changes: No persistent data model changes - badge reads from in-memory UnreadTracker state
api_contracts: CountBadge.init(count: Int) - Initializes badge with display count
UnreadTracker.currentUnreadCount(for sessionId: UUID) -> Int - Returns unread count for session
event_contracts: No new events emitted - badge is purely reactive to existing UnreadTracker state changes
ui_states: BadgeVisible: Count > 0 and session is not active - shows filled capsule with white count text
BadgeHidden: Count = 0 OR session is active - renders EmptyView with zero frame
BadgeOverflow: Count > 99 - displays 99+ text to prevent layout expansion
ui_interactions: Badge appears when background session receives events while user views different session
Badge disappears when user switches to that session (becomes active)
Badge updates count in real-time as new events arrive in background session
edge_cases: EC2: Count of 100 or higher displays 99+
EC3: Session becomes active while badge visible - badge immediately hides
EC4: Rapid count updates do not cause flickering or layout thrashing
EC5: Empty session list renders without errors when no badges to display
failure_modes: FM1: UnreadTracker unavailable - badge renders as hidden with warning log
FM2: Invalid session ID - badge renders as hidden gracefully without crash
rollback_plan: Remove CountBadge.swift file and revert SessionRow.swift changes. Badge feature disabled with no user-facing errors. Sessions sidebar returns to previous appearance without unread indicators.

unit: test_CountBadge_displaysCount_whenPositive: Verify badge shows 5 when initialized with 5
test_CountBadge_displaysOverflow_whenAbove99: Verify badge shows 99+ when initialized with 150
test_CountBadge_hidesCompletely_whenZero: Verify badge returns EmptyView when count is 0
test_CountBadge_accessibilityLabel_includesExactCount: Verify label reads 5 unread events for count 5
integration: test_SessionRow_showsBadge_whenUnreadAndNotActive: Full row renders badge when conditions met
test_SessionRow_hidesBadge_whenActive: Active session row never shows badge regardless of count
test_SessionsSidebar_badgesUpdateOnTrackerChange: Published unread changes propagate to UI
ui: UI_Badge_Visible: Screenshot test showing badge on inactive session with unread events
UI_Badge_Hidden: Screenshot test showing active session without badge
UI_Badge_Theme: Visual comparison of badge in light vs dark theme
perf: test_CountBadge_renderTime_under1ms: Benchmark badge instantiation and body computation

telemetry_events: badge_displayed: Fires when badge becomes visible with session_id and count properties
badge_hidden: Fires when badge hides due to session becoming active

metrics.name: badge_render_count
metrics.notes: Track how often badges are rendered to detect unnecessary re-renders

metrics.name: badge_max_count_displayed
metrics.notes: Track highest unread count shown to validate 99+ overflow logic

log_expectations: WARN UnreadTracker unavailable, badge hidden for session=<id>
acceptance_tests: AT1: Given a background session with 5 new events, when viewing the sessions sidebar, then a badge showing 5 appears on that session row
AT2: Given viewing a session with unread events, when that session becomes active, then the badge immediately disappears
AT3: Given a session with 150 unread events, when viewing the sidebar, then the badge displays 99+ not 150
acceptance_criteria: AC1: CountBadge component exists and compiles without errors
AC2: Badge displays correct count for values 1-99
AC3: Badge displays 99+ for values 100 and above
AC4: Badge is hidden when count is 0
AC5: Badge is hidden for the currently active session
AC6: All unit and integration tests pass
AC7: VoiceOver reads badge count correctly

criteria: SessionRow.swift modified to include badge conditionally
Manual verification shows badge appearing and hiding correctly

completed_when: CountBadge component renders unread counts in SessionRow, hides appropriately for active sessions and zero counts, and all automated tests pass.
completed_evidence: swift test output showing CountBadgeTests and SessionRowTests green. Screenshot of sidebar showing badge on one session row with count visible.
status_reason: Awaiting completion of T001 UnreadTracker service implementation before badge can be integrated.
open_questions: Should badge have subtle animation when count increments?
Should clicking badge navigate to first unread event in that session?
notes: This is a purely presentational component with minimal complexity. Primary risk is layout integration with existing SessionRow structure.

na_justifications.test_plan.security[0]: CountBadge is a read-only display component with no user input, no data mutation, and no network access - no security attack surface exists

verification_steps: Run swift build to verify CountBadge.swift compiles without errors
Run swift test --filter CountBadgeTests to verify all unit tests pass
Run swift test --filter SessionRowTests to verify integration tests pass
Launch app in debug mode with multiple sessions, generate events in background session, verify badge appears with correct count
Switch to session with badge and verify badge disappears immediately

risks: Badge integration may cause SessionRow layout to shift or overflow on narrow sidebars
UnreadTracker service may not be ready when this atom is implemented
Badge visibility logic edge cases may cause flickering during rapid session switches
mitigations: Use fixed max width of 20pt and 99+ overflow to guarantee layout stability
Mock UnreadTracker in tests to decouple from service implementation timeline
Debounce visibility changes or use animation transactions to prevent flicker
risk_register.blast_radius: Isolated to UI layer. Affects SessionRow and sidebar visual appearance only. No impact on session data, event processing, or other features.
risk_register.fallback_plan: Delete CountBadge.swift and revert SessionRow changes. Feature gracefully degrades to no badge display. No data loss or functional regression.

state: CountBadge reads count from UnreadTracker published property
persistence: No persistence - badge state is ephemeral and derived from in-memory UnreadTracker
